description:
CLOSES THREE HOLES IN AN EDGE-TRIGGERED ALERT.

1. The other alarm automations fire once, on off->on, and never again. A shutdown at 2am sends exactly one push; miss it and nothing ever mentions it again, while the generator sits unable to carry an outage. 'No standby power' is a STATE, not an event, and a state deserves a nag.

2. Those triggers require from:'off'. After a Home Assistant restart an already-active alarm goes unavailable->on, which is not off->on, so it is never announced. The homeassistant.start trigger here reconciles that.

3. An alarm that occurs while Home Assistant is down is written to the bridge's flash log and replayed into the recorder, but statistics are not notifications. On restart this sees the alarm is still asserted and says so.

Escalates rather than nags uniformly: critical only when the utility is ALSO down, because a faulted generator during an outage is an emergency and a faulted generator on a sunny afternoon is an errand.
